newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech President's surgeons better off as mechanics.
newsitem.headline: Czech President's surgeons better off as mechanics.

text.p: Doctors who performed lung surgery on Czech President Vaclav Havel earlier this week earned a lower hourly wage for the three-hour operation than the mechanics who work on his official car.

The daily Mlada Fronta Dnes on Wednesday reported that the team of doctors that removed a small malignant tumour from Havel and took out half of his right lung were each paid a collective fee of about 2,200 crowns ($80) for their efforts.
Havel's mechanics are paid about 1,400 crowns ($52) an hour to work on his official car, a Mercedes-Benz.

Under communism, doctors in the Czech Republic were traditionally paid less than blue collar workers such as miners, and continue to earn far less than many workers as the government tries to contain burgeoning health care costs.
Doctors's salaries currently average about 18,000 crowns ($656) a month, approximately twice the Czech average.
The 60-year-old President in convalescing after the operation, and is expected to make a full recovery.
